subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: Which identity is authoritative for approving fallback requests in QQBot C2C conversations when execApprovals is not explicitly configured?
rationale: Current QQBot policy permits public direct messages, so source inspection cannot safely equate every C2C sender with the bot owner; maintainers must choose the intended approval trust contract.

options.title: Require a trusted C2C approver
options.body: Preserve the existing command-authorization gate and resolve approval authority from configured approvers, command owners, or an equally explicit paired-owner identity.

options.title: Authorize every direct sender
options.body: Intentionally treat every sender admitted by the DM policy as an approver, accepting that open-DM users can approve privileged operations.

options.title: Keep the current denial behavior
options.body: Close or pause this PR and document that users must configure a concrete allowFrom entry or execApprovals.approvers for native fallback buttons.

recommendation.title: Require a trusted C2C approver
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing command-authorization gate and resolve approval authority from configured approvers, command owners, or an equally explicit paired-owner identity.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed, repaired, proved, and merged the current QQBot fallback authorization contract.
